describes: A face stone of a dry wall of split slate (port step 2b, R2a; the design's SN2, SN4, SN5 and SN10): a rigid convex block on its natural bed, its top and bed the laminae's planes, its face split across them at the wall's batter in one plane or two (a convex bulge whose edges lie on the wall's plane), its ends split; set into its cell from R1's laying by a seeded half joint on each side. Only what is seen is drawn: the face, and of its top, bed and ends a band behind the wall's plane as deep as a joint is seen. L0 chamfers the face's arrises with its top and its ends; its bed's stays square (SN7: that chamfer would face down, a dark line beneath the edge), and the arrises that run back into the wall lie in its joints and stay square.

chamferMm.note: SN4's 10 to 12 at its top. SN4 asks at least 2 px at 8 m, and the face's end chamfers are seen about 50 degrees off their normal in the judging view, where a 10 mm leg is 1.9 px and 11 mm leaves a two-facet face's lower piece under 2 (every sixth pool stone: 19.9%, 1.2% and 0% thin at 10, 11 and 12; reviews/lt1/port/2b/r2a/stones/blender.md).

chamferMeasure.note: Measured along each face, as a mason gives it (C10); 'face' (the chamfer's width) is not built.

arrisMaxDeg.note: Two faces meeting at a turn of 20 degrees or more meet at an arris (a face's own facets never do: they are one face).

faceFacets.note: SN4: a face's planes, weighted [count, weight]: most faces one plane, one in four broken once; L1's 16 triangles allow no third (its ends would take four each).

facetStepMm.note: SN4: a facet stepped back 15 to 25 mm (a seeded whole mm) where laminae broke.

facetLeastMm.note: SN9: no face under 50 mm; every facet is a lamina at least this high.

bedChamfer.note: The bed's arrises square: a chamfer there faces down, the dark line beneath an edge SN7 forbids, and SN8's thin piece at 8 m (blender.md, the bed arris); true is the arm for R2a's A/B.

bandMarginPerMille.note: The drawn band clears SN8's 2 px by this, per mille, in the gate's view (the top of a tall stone sits a little above the view's target, seen a little flatter).

patches.note: The face patches (blender/parts/stone/slate/patches.manifest.json; SN6) each kind of face draws one from by seed: a split face from the split ones, the top and bed (bed faces) from the bed ones.

note: Sizes from R1's walling table (packs/stavanger-1989/walling.json, the dry-split-1874 working) and its laying: w a cell's length (shortMm 120 where a run leaves no whole stone, to stoneMm's 850) less its two half joints (2 to 6 mm each), h a course (courseMm 120 to 260) less its two; d half the wall's top (wall.py's 420 mm), a hidden back that changes nothing drawn (only a band about 70 mm deep behind the face is). Levels: the design's SN8 budgets per piece (40 and 16); their errors are the wall kind's (kinds/wall.json: levels), the one source (design.md SN8): L1 is the same planes without L0's chamfers, so its error is the chamfers' (8.5 mm on an arris at a 12 mm leg, 9.2 mm at the top corners, where two meet). L2 to L4 are the chunk's (the port's step 5). The part's own numbers are its params, each with its reason; the working's (joints, batter, the top's thickness) are walling.json's (reviews/lt1/port/2b/r2a/stones/blender.md, Data and code).
